    Overwrite a cohort's placeholders with the gold standard

    Source: R/gold-standard.R
    sdt_apply_gold_standard.Rd

    Joins the gold-standard codebook onto a cohort, or onto any frame carrying a card id, and replaces the named columns with the deck's own values. The replaced columns are kept as <col>_original, so the provenance is not lost and the inference that was there before can still be scored against the truth that replaced it.

    Usage

    sdt_apply_gold_standard(
  cohort,
  gold,
  on = "card",
  replace = c("triage", "age", "sex"),
  keep_original = TRUE
)

    Arguments

    cohort

    A cohort from sdt_cohort(), or any data frame with a card id column.

    gold

    An sdt_gold_standard from sdt_read_gold_standard().

    on

    Name of the card id column in cohort. Values may be padded ("07"), unpadded ("7") or numeric; all three join.

    replace

    Which columns to overwrite: any of "triage", "age" and "sex". Pass character() to join nothing and only stamp triage_source.

    keep_original

    Keep each replaced column as <col>_original.

    Value

    cohort with the named columns replaced, the originals kept when asked for, and a triage_source column reading "gold". A cohort comes back a validated cohort; anything else comes back a tibble::tibble(). The gold_applied attribute records what was done.

    Details

    In the TDSC corpus the three replaceable columns start out as a circular surrogate (triage, the inter-team consensus call), a constant (age) and an inference from the log's gendered wording (sex). After this function they are the card's own values, and triage_source reads "gold" so a downstream result can say which label it routed on. The engine routes on triage, so which label sits there decides which question a simulation answers.

    Provenance

    triage_source names where the label sitting in triage came from, so it reads "gold" only when triage was among the columns replaced. Ask for a subset that leaves triage alone and any existing source label is left alone with it: a surrogate must never end up wearing the truth's label.

    See also

    sdt_read_gold_standard(), sdt_triage_accuracy().

    Examples

    if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
gold <- sdt_read_gold_standard("Patienten Codebook.xlsx")
truth <- sdt_apply_gold_standard(pooled, gold)
mean(truth$triage == truth$triage_original)
} # }
